mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE rising by at least 0.4pp.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by > -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of two consecutive months with INDPRO falling by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 3% accompanied by a concurrent rise in the consumer price index above 3% monthly suggests a policy-lag environment where monetary easing fails to curb inflation, leading to elevated uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during months when FEDFUNDS < 3% and CPIAUCSL > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above 5% for four consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and labor, supporting corporate earnings and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month by > 5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months with HOUST rising by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) acceleration above 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with PAYEMS growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 2% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based collapse in household demand, which depresses corporate revenues and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline by > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during months when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall by more than 2%.
